title: Planning Dimension
description: This section shows how tawilis-based agri-tourism is organized and promoted, covering stakeholder collaboration, social media promotion, and the information that helps you learn about and explore tawilis-related attractions before you visit.
paragraphs: Tawilis-based agri-tourism activities in Agoncillo are jointly organized by the local government, fisherfolk, local tourism officers, tour operators, and local tourism businesses, so the community works together to welcome visitors. Social media platforms and different organizations are also used to share facts and updates about Sardinella tawilis, so following them is a good way to stay informed. Clear information about rates, schedules, and tawilis-related activities is available even before you visit, which makes trip planning easier. Tawilis is also featured in Agoncillo’s promotional materials, such as brochures, tour packages, and local events, and you may coordinate with the LGU of Agoncillo to get a copy. Agoncillo likewise has local ordinances and guidelines that support the development of tawilis-based agri-tourism.
heading: Planning your visit

title: Physical Dimension
description: This section highlights the infrastructures and facilities that are available and support tawilis-based tourism, such as transportation, amenities, and signage.
paragraphs: There are safe and accessible roads and transportation to reach tawilis fishing communities. These roads are open to both public and private vehicles.
Private Transportation: You can use Google Maps to access the designated road map.
Public Transportation: You can ride jeepneys or tricycles and tell the driver your desired destination.

Once you arrive, proper facilities such as restrooms, resting areas, and dining areas are available at tawilis-related sites to accommodate tourists’ comfort, so you can relax and enjoy your visit. Safe boating and viewing areas are also provided for tourists, giving you a chance to appreciate Taal Lake up close. If you want to have this kind of experience, kindly coordinate with the LGU of Agoncillo, they will accompany you. Clear signage and directions at tawilis-related sites will guide you to your desired destinations, and designated parking areas are available for tourists’ comfort and safety.
heading: Getting here

title: Agricultural Dimension
description: This section invites you to learn by experiencing, from understanding local fishing activities and why tawilis matters to the Taal Lake fishery, to appreciating the people and traditions behind it.
paragraphs: Tawilis from Taal Lake is an aquatic resource closely tied to the local fishing activities in Agoncillo, and it is part of the daily life of many fishing families. Sustainable fishing practices for tawilis can be part of agri-tourism education for visitors, along with information about responsible tawilis fishing that helps tourists understand why protecting fishery resources matters. Tourists can also join simple fishery-related activities under the guidance of local fisherfolk, so you can learn directly from the people who know the lake best. Coordinate with the LGU of Agoncillo to arrange this. Souvenir products made from tawilis are also available, so you can take home a piece of your experience.
heading: Fishing with the community

title: Socio-Cultural Dimension
description: This section highlights the cultural significance of tawilis in Agoncillo, from local traditions and cuisine to the festival that celebrates it.
paragraphs: Tawilis is part of local traditions in Agoncillo and serves as the municipality’s local symbol, a reminder of how closely the community’s identity is tied to Taal Lake. Dishes made from tawilis are part of the traditional cuisine and food culture of Batangas, so tasting them is a way to experience the local heritage. Agoncillo also celebrates the Tawilis Festival, which honors the fish and the harvests of Taal Lake. Knowledge and stories about tawilis continue to contribute to the cultural identity of Agoncillo, and the locals are often happy to share them with curious visitors.
heading: Food and the Tawilis Festival

title: Environmental Dimension
description: This section highlights why tawilis is special: it is found in Taal Lake and nowhere else. It also shows how visitors can help protect the lake and the fish that call it home.
paragraphs: Tawilis found in Taal Lake is part of the natural aquatic resources of Agoncillo, and it is a type of sardine closely associated with the local food culture. It is endemic to Taal Lake, an important natural resource for the communities of Agoncillo, and it is the world’s only known freshwater sardine species, which makes it part of the area’s natural heritage. Its natural habitat is limited to Taal Lake, so protecting the lake also protects the fish. Because tawilis is an endangered species, visitors can help by keeping the lake clean, taking their trash with them, and following local guidelines during their visit.
heading: Caring for Taal Lake

title: Economic Dimension
description: This section shows how tawilis supports the Agoncillo community through livelihoods, local products, and affordable experiences for visitors.
paragraphs: Tawilis is one of the sources of income in Agoncillo, and it is sold in local markets and nearby areas such as Tagaytay, Cavite, and Manila. A variety of local products featuring tawilis are available to tourists, including foods and products at reasonable prices, and there are tawilis-based food products that provide affordable dining options for visitors. Every purchase you make helps support local fisherfolk and families. Agoncillo also offers informational brochures highlighting the municipality’s attractions and local identity, including tawilis. Visitors interested in obtaining these materials may coordinate with the LGU of Agoncillo.
heading: Local products
